title: performance-canary-automated-detection-rollout-guards-latency-throughput-thresholds
author: Priya Raman
description: Motivation: Improve reliability of performance canaries by adding automated detection for simultaneous latency and throughput regressions, KV-cache-aware thresholding, and rollout guards with hysteresis to avoid flapping. This PR implements an enhanced canary detector that reasons about p50/p95/p99 latency and request-level throughput changes, applies adaptive thresholds based on historical variance, and enforces rollout guards (min-sample, sustained-failure-window, and automatic rollback). Checklist: - [x] Implement detector algorithm and configuration schema - [x] Add canary metrics aggregation pipeline (per-model, per-route) - [x] KV cache sensitivity adjustments (separate thresholds for cold/hot cache) - [x] Hysteresis and recovery policy for rollout decisions - [x] Integration tests + synthetic workload canary job - [x] End-to-end smoke tests against perf-canary lab - [x] Docs: console UI + operator notes Context: We observed two recent incidents where small throughput regressions coinciding with higher tail latency caused canaries to oscillate and either delay or prematurely abort rollouts (see linked Linear tasks). The previous detector treated latency and throughput signals independently which led to false positives during traffic shifts and cache warmup. This change centralizes detection logic to reason about joint regressions, includes minimum-sample-size guards, and integrates KV-cache state from the serving runtime to select appropriate thresholds. Backwards compatibility: The new detector is feature-flagged and uses existing canary config with optional new fields; operators can opt into the adaptive mode per-environment. Related: ENG-4821, SRE-213. Testing notes: Added unit tests for detector math, end-to-end canary run in perf-canary lab (two synthetic workloads: steady-state and cache-warmup ramp), and manual verification using the canary UI. Performance: Minimal CPU overhead in metrics aggregator (~3% at 1k TPS) measured in perf-canary lab; telemetry shows no impact to production dashboards during feature-flag rollout. Merge: Squash merge after approvals and CI green.
